questions.question: When a driver enters public traffic from a driveway or private road, what should they do?

options.text: Yield to drivers already on the public road.
Assume other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you must yield to drivers already on the public road. Wait for a safe gap and merge slowly.

questions.question: When turning left, which traffic signal gives you the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: A green left arrow means you can turn left in that direction. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect how far it takes to stop your vehicle?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change based on your speed and road conditions.

questions.question: What does a speed restriction sign show?

options.text: Can be ignored in rain, snow, or ice.
A recommended speed for a curve or turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: A recommended speed for a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: Signs on curves and turns show a recommended safe speed. Even if you feel safe driving faster in good weather, always slow down in rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: What factors determine how much space you need to cross traffic?

options.text: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic
The presence of a stop sign

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather, and how much oncoming traffic there is.

questions.question: When should you NOT pass another vehicle?

options.text: When school bus lights are flashing

questions.explanation: Never pass on hills, curves, at intersections, near railroad crossings, or on bridges. Also, do not pass a school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop, then proceed when the way is clear
Stop and wait for a green light or green arrow
You can turn in the direction the arrow points

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for a green light or green arrow
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop completely. Wait until a green light or green arrow appears before moving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: When you see a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line with the broken line next to your lane, when can you pass?
questions.explanation: When the broken yellow line is next to your lane, you can cross to pass if no oncoming traffic is coming.

questions.question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?

options.text: Early enough so others know your plans

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so others know your plans
questions.explanation: Signal early when passing so other drivers can see your intentions in advance.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop?
questions.explanation: Road condition greatly affects how quickly you can stop. On slippery or poor roads, you must slow down to stay in control. If you drive too fast on bad roads, you may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.explanation: Larger vehicles have larger blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas behind them that cannot be seen in their mirrors.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator sticks while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift into neutral and press the brake pedal steadily. Then safely pull off the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: What affects how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach.
How much time passes between drinks.

questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Food in your stomach slows alcohol absorption but cannot prevent impairment from too much drinking.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on a freeway shoulder?

options.text: As long as you turn on your emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to check a map for directions.

questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except in an emergency situation.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
Passing poor drivers by moving ahead of them in traffic.
Following the car in front of you closely.
Quickly changing lanes and moving in and out of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means recognizing dangerous situations and taking action before an accident happens. It helps you avoid problems with aggressive, careless, or impaired drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that the right lane is ending. All traffic in that lane must move left.

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always:
questions.explanation: All octagonal signs are stop signs. Come to a complete stop when you see a red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The left lane is reserved for vehicles with a certain number of people in them.
Only certain turns are allowed from certain lanes.
Both lanes must merge smoothly together.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane is reserved for vehicles with a certain number of people in them.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane. These lanes are only for buses and vehicles with the required number of passengers shown on the sign.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time, who goes first?

options.text: One driver can go without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.explanation: If you arrive at an intersection at the same time as a vehicle on your right, that vehicle has the right-of-way. Yield to them and proceed when safe.

questions.question: To be ready for hazards ahead, you should:

options.text: Look at the entire road and all sides.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Focus only on the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and all sides.
questions.explanation: Handling dangerous situations depends on seeing problems before you reach them. Look far ahead, but also scan the sides of the road. Do not just stare at the center.

questions.question: A steady yellow light means a ____ light will appear soon.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light warns you that a steady red light is coming next.

questions.question: To reduce tiredness on a long drive, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Switch feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop for a short break every two hours on long trips. If you feel drowsy, pull over safely and rest or sleep.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or entering traffic from an alley or parking area. This tells other drivers what you are doing and prevents accidents.

questions.question: Highway signs that require drivers to obey instructions are called:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must do. Breaking the rules on these signs can result in a penalty.

questions.question: Before you start the engine, you should:

options.text: Make sure only backseat passengers have their seat belts on.
Make sure only adults have their seat belts on.
Make sure only children have their seat belts on.
Make sure everyone in the car has their seat belt on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure everyone in the car has their seat belt on.
questions.explanation: Before starting the car, buckle your seat belt and make sure all passengers buckle theirs.

questions.question: A flashing red light means:

options.text: The same as a stop sign.
You do not need to stop completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for pedestrians and traffic, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true after drinking?

options.text: Your ability to judge speed and distance gets worse.
You calm down and focus better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and focus better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, worsens your vision, distorts your judgment of speed and distance, and makes you less careful and more willing to take risks.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that bicycles may be in the area.

questions.question: On a road without sidewalks, pedestrians should walk on the:
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road facing the traffic nearest to them.
